title: The Founding Mothers
subtitle: The origin story — almost two hundred years of a real science, built leap after leap by the women the textbook forgot to name.
lesson: AI was never one thing, and never new — it's a real science almost two hundred years old, built leap after leap by women. Every major advance (the algorithm, frequency-hopping, the compiler, search, computer vision) has a woman's name on it.
emotionalBeat: Overwhelm becomes belonging: she stops feeling behind the moment she learns it took almost two hundred years and a hundred brilliant women to hand it to her.
oneLineDescription: The one in which she realizes she's talked to AI every day for weeks with no idea where it came from — goes looking for the origin story, and finds out it was women all along.
episodeDescription: A flashback episode. Three weeks in, our heroine realizes she has no idea where AI came from — so she goes up to the quiet wing of the LUMINAiRY, meets the MAiVENS, and hears the whole origin story: Ada Lovelace, Hedy Lamarr, Grace Hopper, Karen Spärck Jones, Fei-Fei Li, and the women who now check the whole machine. AI turns out to be almost two hundred years old — and built, leap after leap, by women.
previously: She learned that a polished, confident AI answer can still contain one quiet, confident lie — so she checks it like Elle Woods before her name goes on anything.
tryOn: No try-on this week — a field trip. Go up to the LUMINAiRY, walk into the quiet wing, meet one MAiVEN you'd genuinely never heard of before today, and text one friend a single sentence about her.
mainCharacterEnergy: You were never behind on AI — you were just never told it was yours.
